title: Canonical completeness of bounded projective sheaf tensors
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and use $D(B_T)$, the unbounded derived category of $B_T$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For $H\in D(B_T)$ put $C_T(H)=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(H\otimes^L_{B_T}(A_n)_T)$, with strict quotient transitions, restriction of scalars along $B_T\to(A_n)_T$, and the functorial product mapping-fiber model [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Write $\eta_H:H\to C_T(H)$ for the canonical quotient augmentation (zero shifted-product coordinate) [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

The functor $C_T:D(B_T)\to D(B_T)$ is additive and exact as a functor of triangulated categories, with its natural unit $\eta$, and $\eta_{B_T[0]}$ is an isomorphism. For every bounded complex $P$ of $B_T$-module sheaves whose terms are direct summands of finite sums of $B_T$, the map $\eta_{[P]}$ is an isomorphism. Here a direct summand is specified by an inclusion into $B_T^{\oplus r}$ and a retraction with identity composite.

For any two such bounded complexes $P,Q$, their direct-sum total tensor $V=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{B_T}Q)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is bounded and again has terms of this form. Its terms are flat and $P,Q,V$ are K-flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. Consequently $[V]$ represents the ordinary derived tensor $[P]\otimes^L_{B_T}[Q]$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and $\eta_{[V]}$ is an isomorphism. These conclusions apply to sheaf summands and arbitrary sheaf-linear differentials, without requiring constant projective $R$-module models.

proof.text: Use normalized quotient-completion exactness with its shift-compatible actual unit, and the separate rank-one coefficient calculation. These give an additive exact endofunctor F and shift-compatible eta with eta at B[0] invertible.

Finite products of B identify with finite biproducts and hence are flat. Flatness is closed under retracts. The specified splittings therefore make every term of P and Q flat. The bounded-above-flat K-flat theorem makes both complexes K-flat, with no constant module presentation.

The iso locus of eta is closed under finite products and retracts. Naturality on the specified inclusion and projection proves invertibility for every term in degree zero. Apply the existing proved source theorem DerivedCategory.isIso_app_Q_obj_of_isStrictlyGE_of_isStrictlyLE_of_prop (WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.FlatDevissage). Its brutal-truncation induction and shift compatibility prove invertibility for P. The arbitrary differentials and the cases of empty support and zero ranks are covered.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.5; bounded stupid-truncation devissage, source library FlatDevissage

proof.text: Tensor the specified splittings termwise, distribute tensor over finite biproducts and use the unitors. Thus P^p tensor Q^q is a retract of a finite product of B. In degree k the total tensor is a finite biproduct: keep precisely pairs (p,q) with p+q=k and p in the finite interval supporting P; the remaining summands are zero. Explicit inclusions into the totalization and its universal desc map give inverse composites. Summing the finite splittings gives the required finite-product retract for each total term. The usual total-tensor support bounds give [a+c,b+d].

source.place: Lemma 6.5.5 tensor finite-projective reduction; finite totalization

proof.text: Apply the existing K-flat total tensor model to P,Q: its conclusions provide flat total terms, K-flatness of the total tensor, and its derived tensor representative isomorphism. Finally apply the same bounded iso-locus devissage to the total tensor, using the bounds and finite retracts just constructed.

The item is a statement-only node created on 2026-10-22 by Q134; it is not a re-split item, since no repair note exists. The statement is kept verbatim and the delivery adds 8 steps and no new nodes. Source: Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.5.5, pp. 49–50, which reduces through direct summands of finite free complexes; the item is the agent-written sheaf-retract version of that step. Coefficients are B_T = lim (A_n)_T on the pro-étale site in the unbounded D(Mod B_T). This agrees with def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients and with the citer lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion, which uses the same product mapping-fiber model with zero shifted coordinate. Step 1: summand flatness via retracts of exact sequences, and the tensor retract onto B^{rs}, both checked. Step 2: the bounded-flat K-flat lemma and the tensor-descent representative isomorphism. Step 3: I recomputed the homotopy formula H(h) = (hv, -hu); it works because h commutes with s. Step 4: the hypotheses of lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class come from the K-flat resolution lemma and lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings (1) plus the Roos lemma; lem-pe-kflat-scalar-tower-realization supplies the units and transitions, and the unit descends by the localization universal property. Step 5: Roos augmentation, cone and shift clauses; reduction to good cone triangles via a roof plus a K-flat resolution; the cone of good complexes is good via the tensor-cone iso and the acyclic-cone criterion; then two-out-of-three. Step 6: I computed H of a degree-0 surjective tower (kernel lim, cokernel 0), using the free-cell ordinary-limit lemma with r=1, d=0 and the surjective-tower lemma (1). Step 7: both composites of q η^{-1} C_T(j) verified. Step 8: brutal-truncation descending induction. Small cases checked: empty T, r=0, the zero complex, P=[B -ϖ-> B]. Duplicate search found nothing that states the item: lem-sf-perfect-tensor-roos-completion has constant models; lem-sfb-ringed-complete-triangulated is about the Koszul Λ functor; lem-a1-quotient-unit-shift-completeness covers shifts only. Tool uses: the 9 declared ones are accepted; the undeclared off-unit citations are Lean-closed or Mathlib nodes. No SGA source anywhere.
